name: Ace-To-Five Lowball
description: Ace-To-Five Lowball is a draw poker variant in which the lowest hand wins. Aces are low, and straights and flushes do not count against a low hand.
deck: Standard 52-card deck (some tables allow one joker as a bug)

overview.description: Ace-To-Five Lowball is a draw poker variant in which the lowest hand wins. Aces are low, and straights and flushes do not count against a low hand.
overview.deck: Standard 52-card deck (some tables allow one joker as a bug)

history.origins: Ace-to-five lowball developed in U.S. card rooms and became a core lowball form, especially in California.
timeline: 20th century: California draw lowball rooms popularize ace-to-five ranking.
Modern mixed games: Ace-to-five appears in single-draw and triple-draw formats.
history.cultural: A foundational lowball game in dealer's choice and mixed poker lineups.
history.evolution: Compared with ace-to-six and deuce-to-seven, this form removes straight/flush penalties, making wheel-building central.

setup.players: Two to eight players; the game is similar to Five Card Draw with one draw round. Typically played with blinds (dealer, small blind, big blind) or an ante; best with about six at the table.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck; optional joker bug in some house rules.
setup.dealing: Deal 5 cards face-down to each player.
setup.equipment: Deck, chips, dealer button, and blind markers if blind structure is used.

rules.objective: Make the lowest five-card hand by ace-to-five ranking.
rules.gameplay: Players contribute forced bets (ante or blinds), receive five down cards, complete first betting, perform a single draw (discard 0-5 then draw equal replacements, or stand pat), complete final betting, and go to showdown.
keyRules: Straights and flushes are ignored for low ranking.
Hands are compared from highest card downward among low hands.
In some California rules, made sevens may be forced to bet.

strategy.basic: Prefer smooth lows and avoid drawing to rough one-card gutters.
strategy.intermediate: Use opponent draw counts to estimate made hands versus drawing hands.
strategy.advanced: Apply pressure when pat, and represent made lows in heads-up final betting spots.
tips: A-2-3 starts are strong; rough 9-low draws are often traps.
A pat hand can be value or bluff depending on prior draw pattern.

variations.name: Single Draw
variations.description: One draw round and two main betting rounds.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Base engine already models the single-draw structure; no separate overrides are required.

variations.name: Triple Draw
variations.description: Three draw rounds with additional betting rounds.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Triple-draw format is described in sources, but detailed multi-draw engine overrides are not yet modeled.

scoring.description: Pot game; best low hand wins the pot at showdown.
scoring.winCondition: Lowest valid ace-to-five hand at showdown wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: Draw lowball where aces are low and straights/flushes do not hurt your low hand.
